sources.locator: Delegates in Tucumán declared independence of the United Provinces in 1816 after the 1810 revolution. Original Spanish preamble, 1853 constitution with 1994 amendments and continuing federal republican framework. The so-called Conquest of the Desert was a violent culmination of long relations among Indigenous peoples, settlers and the Argentine state, not conquest of empty land. State-approved military campaigns across Patagonia 1878–85, including 1879 Río Negro expedition. 1884 law established common, free, compulsory, gradual primary education. Tango developed among urban lower classes in Buenos Aires and Montevideo through European, African-descended and criollo cultural exchange. Yerba mate has Guaraní roots; people share a gourd and bombilla in rounds, with one person preparing and serving, though customs vary. Archive preserves evidence of human-rights crimes in 1976–83 military dictatorship and reparations. 1983 election restored democratic civilian government after the 1976 military dictatorship.

sources.locator: Francis assumed an Austrian imperial title in 1804; the Holy Roman Empire ended in 1806. The 1814–15 congress reshaped Europe and reinforced Austria’s major-power role. Vienna and other Habsburg cities saw protests demanding a constitution and political voice. Habsburg lands contained many languages and national movements, especially visible in 1848 and 1867. Girls’ schools and private institutes taught reading, science and other subjects, but access and ideals varied. 1835 water shortages and polluted groundwater; bathrooms and indoor toilets were unequal by district; Alpine pipeline opened only in 1873. In 1847 Ignaz Semmelweis introduced hand cleaning to address childbed fever in Vienna. 1867 transformed empire into Austria-Hungary with two governments and a shared monarch, foreign affairs and military.

Early reign dates and borders remain uncertain. Damaged readings remain debated. Archaeologia Adriatica 4 (2010), pp. 53-59, abstract: cemetery by St George above Kastel Sucurac, reidentification of the bronze fitting and late-eighth/early-ninth-century parallels. The object predates the tenth-century royal title evidence. American Journal of Physical Anthropology 148 (2012), pp. 543-556, DOI 10.1002/ajpa.22070; Table 1 and pp. 548-550: adult samples, early medieval millet interpretation and the distinct Sibenik-Sveti Lovre signal. Table A2 dates selected individuals; its dating ranges differ from the broad site labels, so no precise cemetery lifetime is adopted. Starohrvatska prosvjeta III/35 (2008), English abstract and full study pp. 211-238: ninth- to eleventh-century cemetery, skeletal and dental stress, small sample limitations and uncertain hunting interpretation. Skeletal similarity is not used to assign biological ethnicity. 1102 coronation at Biograd recorded in St Mary's Zadar cartulary; royal titles; Zadar's recognition in 1105 and the church inscription. This is dynastic change, not the disappearance of Croatian kingship or society.

sources.locator: The Mamluk sultanate ended in 1517 when Ottoman forces took Egypt and Syria. Ottoman period 1517–1805; Cairo’s governor, carpets, Bulaq, 1744 fountain-school, 1786 tax conflict and French occupation 1798–1801. Original research on Cairo, Mamluk beys, taxes and Egypt’s eighteenth-century grain, sugar, rice and Yemeni-coffee commerce. Archival study of eighteenth-century village irrigation, peasant expertise, repairs and court petitions over water use. Scholarly architectural catalogue dates the Abd al-Rahman Katkhuda sabil-kuttab by inscription to August 1744; public water and a school occupied different floors. Original research from court and guild records distinguishes physicians, surgeons, barbers, midwives and other healers; care was varied and not a modern universal health service. Appointed Ottoman governor in 1805, Muhammad Ali obtained hereditary rule in 1841; his own reign ended in 1848.

sources.locator: The Crown established a viceroyalty in 1535 after the 1521 conquest; Indigenous communities faced epidemics, coerced labor and imposed institutions but persisted. In 1535 the viceroyalty governed Mexico, Guatemala, the Caribbean, Florida and southwestern North America from Mexico City. Colonial legal records cover New Spain and later Mexican states, with historical jurisdiction extending well beyond modern Mexico. Sixteenth-century epidemic diseases devastated Native communities and disrupted their societies. In 1571 Indigenous Nahuatl officials used a pictorial legal record to complain of mistreatment and underpayment. Nahua students wrote Nahuatl in Latin letters and painted illustrations; a Spanish translation stands beside their text. Silver left New Spain for Asian goods; silk and porcelain came to Acapulco and influenced Mexican arts. Mexico achieved independence in 1821 and inherited most but not all of the viceroyalty; the Philippines and Caribbean were not part of independent Mexico.
